# Planning and roadmap

This chapter is the readable version of the HIIP work plan. The single source of truth remains the workbook `HIIP_full_plan_EN.xlsx`, on its *Master* tab; what appears here is generated from it and is meant for reading and discussion, not for editing.

The plan covers **12 workstreams**, **49 outputs** and **176 tasks**, spread over fortnightly sprints from 3 August 2026 to 30 July 2027. **29** tasks are done (16%) and 6 are in progress; 3 have been abandoned and are kept for the record. All tasks are assigned to the project manager.

Delayed and Critical flags are computed from the dates as of **22 September 2026**, when this chapter was generated.

## How to read this plan

The plan has three levels, and the distinction between them is what makes it usable. A **workstream** produces a product and is the only level with external validation. An **output** is an intermediate delivery that closes within one or two sprints, and is the only level with a definition of done. A **task** is the concrete work: it has no criteria of its own, being specific enough that once carried out it is done.

The separation that matters most is between the **definition of done** and **external validation**. The definition of done is a set of internal criteria under the project manager's control: the output closes when they are met. External validation is acceptance by the client — the TWG-PHC, the TWG-PFM, the Minister, the financiers — with its own date and **outside the project manager's control**. A product can meet every internal criterion and still not be validated.

The plan also records **deadlocks**: local constraints that stop an output from being achieved even when the work is ready to proceed. A deadlock is not a delay in the work; it is the reason the work cannot move.

Some tasks have no output. That is not an omission: they serve the workstream's external validation directly, without passing through an intermediate delivery, and are grouped separately under each workstream.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Statuses and conventions"}

| Level or flag | Meaning |
|:--|:--|
| Task | Backlog (identified) - To do (committed to the sprint) - In progress - Blocked (held up by third parties) - Done - Abandoned. |
| Output | Not started - In progress - Delayed - Critical - Done - Abandoned. |
| Validation | Not started - In progress - Delayed - Critical - Done - Abandoned. |
| Delayed (orange) | The date is less than two weeks away and the work has not started. The colour appears automatically. |
| Critical (red) | The date has passed and the output is not done. The colour appears automatically. |
| Abandoned (grey, struck through) | Output or task no longer part of the plan. Kept for the record; not counted in sprint load. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[28,72]"}

| Column | Meaning |
|:--|:--|
| Sprint | Planned fortnight. Dates on the Sprints tab. 'Recurring' repeats in every sprint; 'TBC' awaits a date. |
| Estimate | Working days. A first approximation, to be corrected with use. |
| Depends on | What must be completed first. If it is not, the task is Blocked, not late. |
| Deadlock | Local constraint preventing the output from being achieved, even when the work is ready to proceed. When filled in, the cell turns purple. |
| Learning | Critical information that emerged while carrying out the task: consequences, new data, problems recognised. Filled in as the work is done and reviewed at the sprint retrospective. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[18,82]"}

:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Escalation rule"}
Learning that changes the plan does not stay in the column: it becomes a change to the definition of done, a new task, or a line in the risk log.
:::

## The workstreams

### TWG-PHC {#ws-twg-phc}

The technical working group for primary health care is the body the rest of the plan answers to: 6 of the other workstreams have their external validation at a TWG-PHC session. Reconstituting it is not one workstream among others but the precondition that governs the calendar. It is also where the plan is currently held up from outside: its work cannot move until the Ministry does.

### HHFA and situational diagnosis {#ws-hhfa-and-situational-diagnosis}

Revised in September 2026. The inter-agency agreement with UNICEF and UNFPA was abandoned and replaced by an approach to GEPE, the Ministry's planning and statistics office. The HHFA becomes a light version built into the Angolan assessment tool already in use, in support of the Health Map (*Mapa Sanitário*), on a December 2026 horizon. Its legacy is a proposal to extend that tool with the HHFA items, so that assessment does not end with the project. The instrument itself is covered in the HHFA part of this notebook.

::: {.callout-warning title="External validation"}
**When:** 18 December 2026  
**Status:** [Not started]{.st-none}

Light HHFA presented and accepted; support to the Health Map (Mapa Sanitário) and to the expansion of the Angolan tool already in use agreed with GEPE
:::
